Done.

## What was wrong

`get_pager_file` wraps the pager stream in `MaybeStripAnsi`, an `io.TextIOWrapper`. When the pager falls back to the borrowed stdout — `PAGER` pointing at a missing binary, or no pager binary installed (`src/click/_termui_impl.py:476`, `:485`, and the equivalents in `_tempfilepager`) — the wrapper is built over `stdout.buffer`. A `TextIOWrapper` closes whatever it wraps when the GC finalizes it, so as soon as `echo_via_pager` returned and dropped its reference, the real stdout buffer was closed and every later `click.echo` raised `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file`.

The `_SkipClose` shim added in #3482 only covers the `_nullpager` path; it never reaches these fallbacks. Verified both before and after:

```
before fix:  underlying binary buffer closed? True
after fix:   underlying binary buffer closed? False
```

## The fix

`MaybeStripAnsi.__del__` now detaches instead of closing — flushing pending output while leaving the borrowed stream open. This mirrors the existing `_NonClosingTextIOWrapper.__del__` idiom in `_compat.py:72`, and covers every pager backend rather than patching the fallback sites one at a time.

## Verification

- New regression test `test_echo_via_pager_leaves_stdout_open` — fails on the pre-fix tree (`assert not text_stream.closed`), passes after, and asserts the paged text plus a subsequent `echo` both land in the file.
- Full suite: 1585 passed, 94 skipped, 1 xfailed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. (mypy isn't installed in this venv, so the type check didn't run.)
- `CHANGES.rst` entry added under the unreleased 8.4.2 section.
